 Raipur, District Raipur Chhattisgarh
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: This appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (for short " MV Act") has been filed challenging the award dated 30.10.2018 passed by the learned First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal of Fourth Additional Tribunal, Raipur (CG) in Claim Case No.84/2018.

entities.text: First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal of Fourth Additional Tribunal, Raipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
By the impugned award, the learned tribunal has awarded Rs.12,79,600/- as compensation to the appellants/claimants with 7.5% interest per annum on account of death of deceased Nata Devguru in an unfortunate accident which took place on 04.04.2013 by rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1/driver by offending vehicle i.e. Trolley bearing Registration No. OR-26-6494,
owned by respondent No.2/owner and insured with respondent No.3/insurance company.
2) As per the pleadings of the claim application filed under Section 166 of the MV Act, the deceased was the Pujari of temple and used to earn Rs.9,000/- per month.
The appellants/claimants being widow, children and parents of the deceased had filed the claim application claiming total compensation of Rs.33,50,000/-.
3) The claim application was resisted by respondents/driver, owner and insurance company of the offending vehicle on various grounds.
4) The learned tribunal on the basis of pleadings of the parties framed issues and after appreciation of evidence and material available on record awarded the compensation as stated above.

Smt. Bhumita Devguru vs Prithviraj Pradhan on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119457627/
2 5) Learned counsel for appellants/claimants submits that the finding with regard to income of the deceased is absolutely unjustified, though the deceased used to earn more than 300/- per day,
therefore the awarded amount ought to be enhanced.

entities.text: Bhumita Devguru vs Prithviraj Pradhan on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The learned claim Tribunal has also erred in awarding the low amount in other head like love and affection, funeral expenses, loss of consortium,
which ought to be enhanced in view of the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme court in the case of Vimal Kanwar & Ors.

Versus Kishore Dan & Ors. reported in 2013 (7) SCC 476.
6) Learned counsel for respondent No.3 supports the award and submits that the compensation has rightly been awarded and does not require any interference by this Court.
7) Heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the record with utmost circumspection.
8)

entities.text: Kishore Dan & Ors. reported in 2013 (7) SCC 476
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of record, this Court finds that the learned Tribunal has rightly assessed the annual income of the deceased as Rs. 72,000/- per annum.
Looking to the age of the deceased which was 32 years at the time of incident tribunal has applied an appropriate multiplier of 16 which is on correct side.
As he was a married man left behind wife, three children and parents, therefore, 1/4th deduction towards personal expenses is also on a correct side.

The tribunal has awarded Rs.
15,000/- towards funeral and Rs. 15000/- for loss of estate and Rs. 40000/- is awarded towards spousal consortium.

However, the tribunal has not granted any amount towards parental consortium to the appellants No. 2 to 4 and filial loss of consortium to the appellants No. 5 & 6 which in the opinion of this Court should be benefited under the head of filial loss of consortium and loss of parental consortium 9) In light of the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors; (2018) 18 SCC 130, this Court is computing the compensation as below:-
 S.N. Particular Awarded by this Court  1. Monthly Income of the 6000/-
 deceased  2. Future prospects @ 40% 2400/-

sentences.text: For the forgoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.
The amount of compensation of Rs.12,79,600/- awarded by the tribunal is enhanced to Rs.14,79,600/-.
Hence, after deducting the amount of Rs.12,79,600 /-, the claimants are held entitled for an additional amount of Rs.2,00,000/-.
The additional amount of compensation shall carry interest @ 6% per anuum from the date of filing of claim application before the Tribunal, till its realization.
Rest of the conditions of impugned award shall remain intact.
11) In the result, appeal is allowed in part and the impugned award modified to the extent as indicated herein-above.
The deposit tribunal shall pass appropriate order with regard to apportionment, investment and disbursement of the enhanced amount of compensation.
